title: Reduction lemma: cartesian unit-iso check transfers to apartment
body_html:
Reduction lemma: from $\BSigma$ to the apartment $A$

Statement

Lemma (Reduction). Let $\mathscr V \in \Cosh^{\mathrm{cart}}_G(\BSigma, R, \phi)$. The unit map $$\mathrm{unit}_\mathscr V : \mathscr V \;\longrightarrow\; \Loc_\phi\bigl(H_0(\BSigma, \mathscr V)\bigr)$$ is an isomorphism in $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ if and only if $(\mathrm{unit}_\mathscr V)_\mathcal F$ is an $R$-module isomorphism for every facet $\mathcal F \subseteq A$.

Equivalently (via (T1)): the condition is that $(\mathrm{unit})_x : \mathscr V_x \to e_x H_0(\BSigma, \mathscr V)$ is an iso for every point $x \in A$. Either formulation suffices.
proof_html:
A morphism in $\Coeff_G(\BSigma, \Phi)$ is an isomorphism iff it is an $R$-module isomorphism on every facet (this is just the definition of isomorphism in a functor category — the values are the $\mathscr V_\mathcal F$, and structure maps invertibility is checked stalkwise). So the question reduces to: for which facets $\mathcal F \in \BSigma$ does $(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F$ need to be checked?

We claim: it is enough to check on facets contained in the apartment $A$.

(a) $G$-orbit reduction

Both source and target of $\mathrm{unit}_\mathscr V$ are $G$-equivariant (this is just (EC3) and the $G$-equivariance of $H_0$). Thus if $\mathcal F' = g \mathcal F$ for some $g \in G$, then $(\mathrm{unit})_{\mathcal F'}$ is obtained from $(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F$ by the action of $g$ on both sides, and hence one is iso iff the other is.

Concretely: the diagram $$\begin{array}{ccc} \mathscr V_\mathcal F & \xrightarrow{(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F} & e_\mathcal F H_0(\BSigma, \mathscr V) \\ \;\;\downarrow g_\mathcal F^\mathscr V & & \;\;\downarrow g \\ \mathscr V_{g\mathcal F} & \xrightarrow{(\mathrm{unit})_{g\mathcal F}} & e_{g\mathcal F} H_0(\BSigma, \mathscr V) \end{array}$$ commutes, with both vertical arrows isomorphisms (by (EC3) and the $G$-action on $H_0$, using (iv) of [[node:coefficient_systems.idempotent_system_from_T_axioms]] for the right column: $e_{g\mathcal F} = g e_\mathcal F g^{-1}$).

So $(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F$ being iso transports along $G$-orbits.

(b) Every $G$-orbit meets $A$

By [[node:coefficient_systems.A_over_K_equivalence]] (the §7.3 equivalence $[A/\mathscr K] \xrightarrow{\sim} [\BSigma/G]$), the inclusion of facets of $A$ into facets of $\BSigma$ induces a bijection between $N$-orbits in $[\![A]\!]$ and $G$-orbits in $[\![\BSigma]\!]$. In particular, every $G$-orbit of facets in $\BSigma$ has a representative inside $A$.

Combining (a) and (b): checking $(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F$ for all $\mathcal F \in \BSigma$ reduces to checking it for $\mathcal F \subseteq A$.

This proves the "iff" of the lemma. $\square$

Remark — what the reduction does not require

Note we have not used:

  • The Bestvina–Savin contraction (Contraction map c: C_d(A) → C_{d+1}(A) (Bestvina–Savin)) — that is used only in the §7.1 resolution theorem and in the subsequent local-map argument, not in this reduction.
  • (F5)–(F6) — the alcove-level structure. We stop at the apartment.
  • The cartesian condition itself — the reduction lemma is purely about $G$-equivariance and the apartment being a QFD for $G$ acting on $\BSigma$. The cartesian condition only enters in the next step, where we evaluate $(\mathrm{unit})_\mathcal F$ at facets $\mathcal F \subseteq A$.

Localization at a chosen point (preparation for §7.2.5)

For the subsequent unit-iso proof, it is useful to also localize the chain complex $C_\bullet(\BSigma, \mathscr V)$ around a chosen point. The following companion observation, used in Proof plan: Cartesian unit-iso via apartment-level system of idempotents step (d), is independent of the reduction lemma above but worth recording here.

Companion lemma. For any $x \in \BSigma$ with $\mathcal F = \mathcal F_x$, $$e_\mathcal F \cdot C_d(\BSigma, \mathscr V) \;\subseteq\; C_d(\BSigma_x, \mathscr V)$$ where $\BSigma_x := K_x \cdot A = \hat K_x \cdot A$. Consequently $$e_\mathcal F \cdot H_0(\BSigma, \mathscr V) = e_\mathcal F \cdot H_0(\BSigma_x, \mathscr V|_{\BSigma_x}).$$

This is [[node:coefficient_systems.support_in_BSx]] specialized to the facet level. Combined with the reduction lemma, it means the entire unit-iso computation lives on $\BSigma_x = \hat K_x A$ — a much smaller geometric object than $\BSigma$, and one fully determined by data on the apartment $A$ plus the $\hat K_x$-action.

Step in the broader proof

This lemma is Step 1 of the §7.2 cartesian unit-iso proof (Proof plan: Cartesian unit-iso via apartment-level system of idempotents). After this reduction:

  1. Step 2: extract abstract idempotent system properties (i)-(v) from (T1)-(T5) — done in [[node:coefficient_systems.idempotent_system_from_T_axioms]].
  2. Step 3: define local maps $\varepsilon^\tau_\sigma$ along taut paths in $A$ — done in Local maps ε^τ_σ along taut paths in the apartment.
  3. Step 4: prove $\varepsilon^\tau_\sigma$ is well-defined (path-independent) — done (Cases C, D) in Local maps ε^τ_σ along taut paths in the apartment.
  4. Step 5: assemble unit-iso using (i)-(v) and the local maps — done via Lanard 4.9 analogue: i_F ∘ ε^E_F = e_F ∘ i_E for adjacent facets and Unit-iso assembly: V_F ≅ e_F H_0 via surjectivity + injectivity.
